svg.title: CYC connected engineering workflow
svg.desc: Twelve responsibilities inside Scout, Build, Verify and Deliver. Arrows connect the work, developer decisions, knowledge inputs, diagnostic returns, separate ready and blocked outcomes, and independent publication and accepted-learning branches. Complete text explanations accompany the diagram.

text.tspan: Common implementation route · 12 responsibilities inside 4 recorded stages

a.aria-label: 1. Define observable success — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Record the outcome, constraints and acceptance criteria.
Skills: Scout · Frame when the goal is unclear

a.aria-label: 2. Select route & risk — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Choose the playbook, checks and review depth.
Skills: Scout · Challenge for high-risk work

a.aria-label: 3. Retrieve matched history — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Find component decisions and prior failed approaches.
Carry the relevant constraints into the plan.

a.aria-label: 4. Revalidate that history — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Compare recorded claims with current code and changes.
Replace stale assumptions before relying on them.
Skills: Context · Understand when evidence conflicts

a.aria-label: 5. Trace impact & choose design — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Follow writers, readers, state and interface contracts.
Name affected consumers and a check for each.
Skills: Impact · Design · Understand as needed

a.aria-label: 6. Explain & settle decisions — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Connect present behavior to the proposed mechanism.
Resolve decisions that could change the solution.
Skills: Scout · Teach only for a requested lesson

a.aria-label: 7. Plan evaluable slices — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Give each slice an observable outcome and check.
High risk: challenge the plan; otherwise proceed.
Skills: Scout · Challenge for high-risk plans

a.aria-label: 8. Build in tested slices — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Reproduce or pin behavior, implement, inspect the diff.
Explain the effect on dependent components.
Skills: Build · Error Ledger when attempts fail

a.aria-label: 9. Retain useful project knowledge — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Update component docs and index when learning is useful.
Keep verified facts; label undecided proposals as pending.
Finalize authorized context and ledger edits before checks.
Skills: Context · Error Ledger for failure history

a.aria-label: 10. Prove tests & verify behavior — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Original-code proof where required; run configured checks.
Exercise affected consumers against stable covered files.

a.aria-label: 11. Review intent & code quality — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Inspect intent, consumers and project conventions.
Resolve or dismiss findings with recorded evidence.
Skills: Verify · Challenge for consequential review

a.aria-label: 12. Account for outcome & learning — read the step explanation

text.tspan: Record criteria, limits, learning and ledger disposition.
Reuse the shared review and explain maintenance.
Skills: Deliver · Context for retained learning

HOST DELIVERY GATE · enforced when the hook is active
Ready: this session’s relevant touched runs are complete and applicable response checks pass.
Blocked: disclose the unfinished outcome with current review evidence and applicable native reply checks.
An actively running unfinished run must continue or be recorded with an appropriate non-running outcome.
Show the candidate, evidence, reasoning and limits.
No completion claim or publication path.
Blocked run: may resume after resolving input.
Exhausted / halted: new run; fresh evidence.
Review the actual change and its evidence. Completion is not human acceptance or permission to publish.
Publication and acceptance of a pending finding are separate decisions.
Reuse the generated review; satisfy project rules.
Requested revisions after completion use a new run.

A completed run is terminal. Later requested revisions start a new scoped run with fresh evidence.
Ordinary path: run start records Scout; run finish batches Build recording, proof, checks, Verify, Deliver and completion.
R1–R4: match source cards to return arrows.
Dots join paths; other crossings stay separate.
Arrows: teal = forward work · amber = recovery · blue = developer decisions · red = unfinished outcome
Dashed purple = knowledge read / write. The 12 responsibilities are not separate runtime states. Other playbooks have their own sequences.
Skills = CYC methods selected as needed, not automatic dispatch. Click a numbered step for its trigger, worked example and expected evidence.
Next task retrieves and revalidates the retained knowledge
